newsitem.title: USA: IPO SPOTLIGHT -- Boston Properties REIT debut.
newsitem.headline: IPO SPOTLIGHT -- Boston Properties REIT debut.

text.p: Wall Street gets the chance to build on Mortimer Zuckerman's real estate successes when Boston Properties Inc debuts on the New York Stock Exchange Wednesday.

The initial public offering of 31.4 million shares of the real estate investment trust is expected to raise between $753 million and $816 million based on an anticipated pricing range of $24 and $26 a share, according to the prospectus.
Analysts expect the shares in the REIT to reap modest premiums in their initial trading.

"If they price it at the 24 range that's where the buyers are," said Vince Slavin, who follows IPOs at Cantor Fitzgerald. "Its got super management, great properties and at 24 its a good deal," Slavin said, adding that the premium would be smaller if the IPO prices higher.

After the offering, company founders Zuckerman and Edward Linde will own a 31.9 percent interest in the company, according to the prospectus. Zuckerman is a Canadian-born businessman who made his fortune in real estate and whose media holdings include the New York Daily News.
The company will own 75 properties in New York, Boston and Washington when the offering is completed. It will have a $300 million line of unsecured credit to finance development and acquisitions.
REITs manage portfolios of real estate or mortgages. Their relatively high dividends, which offer a cushion during market downturns, have made the stocks popular among defensive-minded investors.
According to the prospectus the company plans to pay an annual distribution of $1.62 per share, for a yield of 6.5 percent based on a initial price of $25 per share.
REITs have attracted renewed interest on Wall Street, although perhaps not to the extent of certain periods in the past.

"The door is swinging open to REITs more on a case by case basis on quality," said John Fitzgibbon of the IPO Aftermarket newsletter. "The times you see REITs coming into the market are in flat to lower interest rates."

Merrill Lynch & Co and Goldman, Sachs & Co are lead underwriters on the offering. Other underwriters include Bear, Stearns & Co Inc, Painewebber Inc, Prudential Securities Inc, Morgan Stanley & Co and Smith Barney Inc.

The underwriters have an over-allotment option of up to 3.77 million shares. Proceeds from the sale of the shares will be used to reduce debt and to finance other general corporate needs, the company said.
In 1996, Boston Properties reported total revenue of $204.6 million, down from $255.2 million in 1995.
